title: Emergency Response for Security Teams
overview: This 5-day course equips security managers and teams with the essential knowledge and skills needed for effective incident and emergency management. The course covers a broad range of topics, including emergency response planning, incident investigation, and risk assessment strategies, enabling participants to adopt and apply best practices in emergency management. Practical, up-to-date techniques will be shared that can be directly implemented within participants' respective organizations and security teams.
audience: This course is designed for personnel involved in the strategy, development, implementation, and management of security operations. Security managers, security specialists, risk management professionals, business continuity professionals, and emergency response teams will benefit greatly from this course.
methodology: The course is highly interactive, using group discussions, case studies, and collaborative work. Practical exercises provide participants with the opportunity to apply the advanced knowledge and skills they gain throughout the course, particularly in emergency response situations.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand the role and responsibilities of security personnel in emergency response scenarios.
Manage incidents effectively and collaborate with emergency services during large-scale crisis situations.
Conduct investigations that lead to actionable risk mitigation strategies.
Demonstrate leadership and implement command and control techniques in emergencies.
Communicate effectively under pressure to ensure clear and concise information exchange.

outline.title: Understanding the Threat for Security Personnel in Emergency Response

items.text: Identifying internal and external risk factors
Defining what constitutes an emergency
Understanding the role and duties of security personnel during emergencies
Knowing when to hand over to external agencies
Providing effective situation reports
Defining situational awareness in emergency response
Preparing crisis management plans
Recognizing early warning signs
Reacting appropriately to incidents
Maintaining emotional self-control in high-pressure situations
Managing others effectively in stressful situations
The 5 Cs of Incident Management
Setting up an Incident Control Point and determining equipment requirements
Managing crowd control and interacting with the public
Securing access to the Incident Control Point
Effective communication techniques, including radio communications
Sending and receiving incident reports

outline.title: Collaboration and Partnership with External Agencies

items.text: Managing an Incident Control Centre
Coordinating with emergency services and specialist bodies (e.g., search and rescue, bomb disposal)
Handling various types of emergencies, including:
Fire emergencies
Medical emergencies
Terrorism-related situations
Natural disasters (earthquakes, floods, etc.)
Deciding when to launch an investigation
Collecting both quantitative and qualitative data
Interviewing skills and procedures
Analyzing information and drawing conclusions
Writing investigation reports and making recommendations
Developing and implementing risk assessment strategies
